items.stem: Why should a dbt model reference another model with ref('model_name') instead of the raw table name?

options.text: ref() builds the dependency graph and resolves the correct schema per environment
options.rationale: Correct: ref() lets dbt order the DAG and point to the right object in each environment.

options.text: ref() makes queries run without a warehouse
options.rationale: ref() still requires a warehouse to execute.
ref() affects execution and lineage, not just docs.

items.stem: What does dbt primarily do in the ELT workflow?

options.text: Transforms data already loaded in the warehouse
options.rationale: Correct: dbt is the T in ELT, transforming data that is already in the warehouse.
Extraction is handled by ingestion tools, not dbt.

options.text: Loads raw files into the warehouse
options.rationale: Loading raw data is done by EL tools, not dbt.
dbt does not serve dashboards; BI tools do.

items.explanation: Correct: dbt is the T in ELT, transforming data that is already in the warehouse.

items.stem: Which TWO are generic tests dbt can apply to a column out of the box? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: unique checks for duplicate values in a column.
Correct: not_null checks that a column has no null values.
sort_descending is not a built-in dbt generic test.
auto_cluster is not a dbt generic test.
